title: Quadratic time bound for the candidate
statement: Let $W$ and $M$ be finite machines over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, let $a,b \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every binary input $x$, $W$ outputs the binary expansion of $T(|x|)$ within $b(T(|x|)+1)$ steps; suppose also that $n\le T(n)$ for every $n$, and that $M$ decides $L$ within $aT(n)$ steps. Then the candidate machine built from $W$, $M$, and $a$ decides $L$ within $\bigl(18(a+1)^2+23(a+1)+3b+25\bigr)(T(n)+1)^2$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: For every binary input $x$, $W$ computes the binary digits of $T(|x|)$ within $b(T(|x|)+1)$ steps
replaced:
